notes:
Account background:
- Veridian builds edge telemetry & inference for industrial fleets. Processing live sensor + operator chat (short queries) and automated alert reranking.
- Historically self-hosted, now moving to hybrid dedicated capacity for predictable latency and ops overhead reduction.

Key business asks (from AE / procurement):
- Predictable monthly committed capacity (reserved GPUs) with burst options. Rough sizing target: reserve 10 GPUs (A100/80GB equiv) in primary region, 4 GPUs reserve in DR region, burst to 20 GPUs for seasonal peaks.
- SLAs: 99.95% uptime, p95 latency SLOs for short-chat completions (<64 tokens) at <=250ms. Throughput guarantee: sustainable 600 concurrent chat sessions / 1,200 RPS for embedding lookups during peak.
- Credits / SLA penalties and response times: 30 min P1 response, 4-hour mitigation window for production-impacting incidents.

Technical evaluation notes:
- POC run (us-west) 3/2: sustained throughput test achieved 450 concurrent chat sessions with p95 ~220ms using quantized 13B model variant. 70B quantized variant meets quality but p95 jumped to ~420ms at same concurrency.
- SE recommended route: primary serve on 70B quantized for highest fidelity under normal load; automatic model-variant fallback to 13B/7B quantized under saturation. Routed by policy: latency-first for user-facing chat (drop to 13B when p95 approaching SLO), cost-first for batch embeddings (route to cheaper variant).
- Cache strategy: aggressive prefix/KV caching for operator prompts expected to cut token compute by ~30%. Caveat: cross-region failover will lose hot KV cache unless we replicate — team wants options: async replication (best-effort) vs. warm standby with synced checkpointing.
- Cross-region failover design discussion: use smart routing + DNS with health checks + stateful failover plan. Concerns raised: cold-start latency for large models in DR region (~30–90s) and cache warm-up costs. Proposed mitigations: warm standby (keep 1-2 GPUs hot in DR), pre-warmed model variants (quantized 13B) for near-instant failover, and traffic shaping during transition.

SLA negotiation items (procurement):
- Uptime target: 99.95% (requested). Define maintenance windows and notification cadence.
- Performance SLAs: p95 latency targets for defined request profiles (short-chat, long completion, embeddings). Need explicit measurement method (token lengths, truncation policy, measurement region).
- Capacity guarantees: committed GPU count, burst policy (how long, cold-start behavior), and credit calculation for throttling/queueing-induced latency misses.
- Security/KMS: must support customer-managed keys for data-at-rest in Dedicated and Private, proof-of-work for KMS integration required before sign-off.

Quotes / direct notes from stakeholders:
- "We cannot accept more than 10s of seconds of degradation during failover — operator workflows must stay near-real-time." — Head of Platform (Z. Morales)
- "If the 70B model imposes >2x cost for marginal quality improvement vs 13B, procurement will push aggressively for fallback policies." — Procurement lead

POC results & follow-ups:
- Action: run DR failover drill (non-prod) 3/18 to measure cold-start and cache regeneration time. (SE Lucas owns)
- Action: sizing doc v2 (attached) to include GPU type options (A100 vs A40), NVLink considerations, and estimated costs for warm-standby strategy. (AE Maya to drive)
- Action: Legal to review SLA redlines and security appendix. Expected turn-around 2 weeks.

Blockers (short):
- KMS sandbox access outstanding (security needs test tenant).
- SOC2 on-prem package requested; security team flagged missing audit logs retention detail.
- Procurement wants explicit failover RTO/RPO numbers for Dedicated before locking reserve commitment.
technical_notes:
Model plan:
- Primary model: 70B quantized (highest quality path).
- Fallback variants: 13B quantized, 7B fp16 for extreme saturation.
- Routing policy: latency-first for user chat, cost-first for background reranking.
- KV cache: local primary-region cache + async replication to DR; plan to provide warm-standby to reduce cold-start.
- Monitoring: token-level latency, per-model QPS, cache hit ratio, per-route SLO dashboards.

Capacity planning summary:
- Reserve: 10x A100-class equivalence in primary region; 4x in DR region.
- Burst: allow autoscale up to 20 GPUs for short windows (policy-based).
- Expected baseline throughput: ~600 concurrent short-chat sessions on mixed-model strategy with caching.

Reliability & failover design considerations:
- Cross-region: DNS failover + health checks + traffic mirrors during cutover.
- Model fallback: automated variant fallback with quality tags and telemetry gating (roll back if quality delta > threshold).
- SLA testing: monthly synthetic tests + quarterly DR drills required by customer.
